source.title: Learning General Representation of 12-Lead Electrocardiogram with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The source header identifies version v5, dated 10 Apr 2026.
record.tranche_reason: It varies pretraining data scale and measures downstream task performance, a different measure and setting from language-model held-out loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws as motivation and compares ECG-JEPA pretrained on 180k versus 960k ECG samples. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, or test extrapolation. The scale comparison bears on downstream predictability (V6), not the loss-law claims. Other downstream benchmark results do not compare scale and are not included.
record.test_reason: This is an ECG self-supervised learning methods paper. Its only scale-related result (Appendix A.1, Tables 8–9) compares one fixed-size ECG-JEPArb model pretrained on 180k vs 960k ECGs and reports downstream AUC/F1. The paper has no held-out pretraining loss, no curve over several scales, no fitted law and no extrapolation, so V1–V3, V5 and V7 cannot be assessed. The system is an ECG transformer, not a language model, so the comparison does not measure what V6 names. The added 780k ECGs also come from a different, acute-care distribution (MIMIC-IV-ECG), which confounds scale with data shift. The authors cite scaling laws only as motivation and call the check preliminary. The result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find a slight drop under linear evaluation and very similar fine-tuning performance with the extended set, and conclude that adding MIMIC-IV-ECG does not significantly degrade performance. They also note that the data was added all at once and that model size was not increased, which limits the scaling analysis.
record.recipe_differences: ECG self-supervised pretraining data-scale comparison; ECG downstream metrics rather than language-model held-out loss, model-size/token/compute scaling, or fitted laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies across downstream task, metric, and evaluation mode. The extended set adds MIMIC-IV-ECG all at once; model size was not increased.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed model size, pretraining ECG-JEPArb on 960k ECGs (adding MIMIC-IV-ECG) instead of 180k gives mixed, mostly negligible downstream changes. Linear multi-class scores drop slightly (PTB-XL AUC 0.897→0.879); fine-tuning scores are about equal. No uncertainty is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ECG self-supervised pretraining at fixed model size, a roughly 5x increase in (distribution-shifted) pretraining data does not reliably improve downstream diagnostic performance.

record.problems: Only two dataset-size settings are compared, with the additional data introduced all at once and from a different dataset distribution. The authors did not increase model size. The scale comparison reports downstream scores rather than pretraining loss or a fitted scaling curve, and Tables 8–9 give no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on a tested claim version. The paper's other downstream evaluations compare methods or settings without varying pretraining scale.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss, and no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit and no prediction of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation and no variation of model size.
No depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count.
ECG modality, but only two data sizes and no loss, so the power-law form cannot be tested.
Not a language model. Only two points with distribution-shifted added data; no relation to loss and no trend or predictability.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V6 supports and challenges labels was rejected. V6 is about language-model downstream scaling, and two ECG data points confounded by a distribution shift cannot show predictable improvement. Several rows were also mis-stated: changes of 0.001–0.004 AUC were coded 'reversed' or 'partial', though the authors describe them as negligible or similar. Scaling laws appear only as motivation, citing Kaplan et al.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute sweep.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or parameter/token scaling.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
The ECG modality is studied, but the paper does not test whether a power-law form holds in ECG or another training regime.
Only one comparison of pretraining dataset sizes is reported; no downstream-performance curve, extrapolation, or relationship to pretraining loss is tested.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or comparison of fitting choices is reported.
